how: The index stood 14.0% above its 200-day average after gaining 25.1% in a year. It was the last record close until 24 Aug.
Fear of faster Fed tightening; bond yields rose. The VIX closed above the three-month VIX for the first time.

t: Dow −1,175; VIX more than doubles to 37.32
how: Selling accelerated in the afternoon as products that had bet on calm were forced to buy volatility. XIV fell about 85% after hours.
Credit Suisse terminated the note. JPMorgan estimated about $100bn of selling by volatility-driven funds. A violent two-way session.
−3.8% to 2,581 with the VIX at 33.46. About 60% of stocks were still above their 200-day average.
Fell further in the morning, turned in the early afternoon and closed up. Put/call ratio 1.31. This intraday low was not broken later.
Start of the trade-war overhang that ran through the year.
Worst day since early February; Caterpillar, 3M and Boeing were hit hardest.

t: Second day of trade selling: put/call 1.54
how: A higher put/call reading than in February. Financials and consumer staples made their lows this day.

t: The retest: China retaliates, Amazon attacked
how: The close matched the 8 Feb closing low with the VIX at 23.62 against 33.46. Technology and small caps held above their February lows.

t: Shanghai Composite enters a bear market
how: Down 20% from its January high. US indices went on to new records two months later.

t: US tariffs on $34bn of Chinese goods take effect
how: China answered with tariffs of similar value the same day.

t: Bull market becomes the longest on record
how: By the common count from March 2009. The index had touched a record intraday the day before.
Seven months after the January high. Materials, financials, industrials and staples had not regained theirs.
Its high for the year, three weeks before the S&P 500’s.
Small caps peaked here. By 24 Dec the index was 27.3% below this high (CNBC, from the intraday high).
